hooks.text: A giant star suddenly lost two-thirds of its light.
Skywatchers thought a giant red star was about to explode.
A massive star choked itself out with its own dust.

title: The Giant Star That Blocked Its Own Light
description: In 2019, the famous red supergiant Betelgeuse rapidly dimmed, leading many to believe a supernova was imminent. NASA's Hubble Space Telescope revealed the star had actually blown out a massive cloud of starlight-blocking dust.

beats.text: A giant star suddenly lost two-thirds of its light.

beats.text: Betelgeuse dropped out of the top ten brightest stars in late 2019.

beats.text: Everyone assumed the giant star was about to explode into a supernova.
beats.visual: Artist's concept of a giant red supergiant supernova explosion, 2020

beats.text: When it does detonate, it will shine as bright as a half-Moon.
beats.visual: Artist's concept of a supernova visible in the daytime sky, 2020

beats.text: But the Hubble Space Telescope caught what actually happened.
beats.visual: Hubble Space Telescope operating in Earth orbit, 2009
queries: Hubble Space Telescope in orbit photograph

beats.text: Betelgeuse erupted a superhot plume of material millions of miles out.
beats.visual: Artist's concept of Betelgeuse surface mass ejection, 2020

beats.text: As the gas cooled into dust, it blocked starlight from its own surface.

beats.text: The giant star was just hiding behind its own shadow.
